sectionDescription: Markets, money, work and the ideas moving Botswana’s economy forward.
title: P1bn diamond fund moves from promise to implementation
excerpt: Government and De Beers have advanced an initial P1 billion to the Diamonds for Development Fund, setting the stage for investment beyond mining.
imageAlt: A diamond processing facility in Botswana beneath a clear blue sky
author: BWIRE Business Desk
body: Government and De Beers Group have advanced an initial P1 billion to the Diamonds for Development Fund, marking the fund’s transition from a landmark agreement into its implementation phase.

The partnership is intended to channel diamond wealth into non-mining sectors, unlock additional domestic and international capital, and support sustainable employment. Its backers describe it as a strategic instrument for economic transformation rather than a short-term stimulus measure.
The fund has completed its structural framework and appointed development economist and former African Development Bank president Dr Akinwumi Adesina to chair its 10-member independent board.

The central test now is execution: which industries receive backing, how projects are selected and whether new enterprises can create durable jobs. The fund’s mandate includes diversification, industrialisation, export competitiveness and broader participation in the economy.
For a country whose modern prosperity was built on diamonds, the initiative represents both continuity and a deliberate turn towards what comes next.
keyPoints: P1 billion has been advanced as initial capital.
The fund will back economic activity beyond mining.
Dr Akinwumi Adesina chairs an independent 10-member board.

sectionDescription: The essential national stories, clearly reported and put in context.
title: Dr Moeti honoured for a lifetime in public health
excerpt: The University of Botswana has recognised Dr Matshidiso Moeti’s leadership and her contribution to stronger health systems across Africa.
imageAlt: Dr Matshidiso Moeti standing beside a World Health Organisation flag
author: BWIRE Newsroom
body: The University of Botswana has honoured former World Health Organisation Regional Director for Africa, Dr Matshidiso Moeti, with an honorary Doctor of Science degree in recognition of her distinguished public health leadership.

Vice Chancellor Professor David Norris conferred the degree during the university’s graduation ceremony. The honour recognises Moeti’s contribution to stronger, more resilient health systems across the continent.

Moeti served as the first woman Regional Director for the WHO African Region from 2015 to 2025. Her tenure included a transformation agenda focused on emergency preparedness, universal health coverage, accountability and women’s leadership.
Her work spanned profound public health challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic, which tested the readiness and resilience of health systems around the world.
keyPoints: Dr Moeti received an honorary Doctor of Science degree.
She was the WHO African Region’s first woman Regional Director.
Her decade in office focused on resilient and equitable health systems.

sectionDescription: Digital life, innovation and the technology changing how Botswana works.
title: Cybercrime awareness campaign puts prevention first
excerpt: The Twantsho Botsotsi campaign calls for shared vigilance as criminals increasingly target people through digital channels.
imageAlt: A digital skills facilitator speaking to a classroom in Botswana
author: BWIRE Digital Desk
body: A national cybercrime awareness campaign launched in Mochudi is urging Batswana to treat online safety as a shared responsibility.

Speaking at the Twantsho Botsotsi launch, Minister for State President, Defence and Security Moeti Mohwasa warned that criminals no longer need physical access to a home or business to cause serious harm.
The campaign places practical prevention at the centre of the response: protecting personal information, recognising suspicious approaches and reporting incidents early.
As more services, payments and conversations move online, digital literacy is becoming an essential form of public infrastructure.
keyPoints: The awareness campaign was launched in Mochudi.
It emphasises vigilance, prevention and reporting.
Digital safety is framed as a shared public responsibility.

sectionDescription: Power, policy and accountability — with the national interest in focus.
title: BNF shifts its policy focus to economic emancipation
excerpt: President Duma Boko has urged the party to align its policies with the demands of governing and Botswana’s broader economic goals.
imageAlt: President Duma Boko at a regional diplomatic meeting
author: BWIRE Politics Desk
body: President Advocate Duma Boko has called for a review of Botswana National Front policies to align them with the demands of governing and the broader goal of economic emancipation.
Addressing delegates at the party’s Special Policy Conference in Selebi Phikwe, Boko said policy needed to respond to present economic realities while retaining a clear focus on expanded opportunity.
The discussion places jobs, productive enterprise and the practical work of government at the centre of the party’s next phase.
For delegates, the challenge is to convert broad political commitments into measurable programmes that citizens can assess.

sectionDescription: The athletes, clubs and competitions carrying Botswana’s sporting ambition.
title: Second bite at the cherry for Team Botswana
excerpt: Three relay teams carry hopes of qualification into a high-stakes repechage round, with only the top two in each heat advancing.
imageAlt: Letsile Tebogo celebrating with supporters at an athletics stadium
author: BWIRE Sport
body: Team Botswana returned to the track carrying the weight of expectation and the promise of redemption as three relay teams lined up in the repechage round.

The format offers a second chance to teams that missed automatic qualification in the heats. The stakes could hardly be higher: only the top two in each heat advance to the World Athletics Championships in Beijing.
Botswana’s campaign included the mixed 4x100m, mixed 4x400m and women’s 4x100m teams, each facing a deep international field.
The mission was simple to describe and difficult to deliver — seize the second chance, finish in the top two and book a place on the global stage.
keyPoints: Three Botswana relay teams entered the repechage.
Only the top two teams in each heat could advance.
A place at the World Athletics Championships was at stake.

sectionDescription: Markets, money, work and the ideas moving Botswana’s economy forward.
title: Economic revival needs a collective national effort
excerpt: President Duma Boko says diversification, manufacturing and new energy capacity must form part of a broader strategy for growth.
imageAlt: A view across Gaborone with hills in the distance
author: BWIRE Business Desk
body: President Advocate Duma Boko says collective strategies are needed from Batswana to revive the country’s economy and widen its productive base.
Speaking at the International Workers Day commemoration in Letlhakane, he argued that Botswana’s long reliance on diamonds had left the economy insufficiently diversified.

Manufacturing, employment creation and sustainable diversification were presented as connected priorities. The President also pointed to the Maun 500MW Solar Photovoltaic Plant as an opportunity to reduce electricity imports and retain more public funds.
Union representatives used the same platform to press for wage improvements and stronger cooperation with government as households contend with rising costs.

sectionDescription: Power, policy and accountability — with the national interest in focus.
title: Botswana seeks global expertise to advance media reforms
excerpt: International technical cooperation is expected to support legislative reform, journalist protection and sustainable independent journalism.
imageAlt: An aerial view of Botswana’s landscape and settlements
author: BWIRE Politics Desk
body: Botswana has sought international technical cooperation to strengthen media legislative reforms, protect journalists and promote sustainable independent journalism.
The engagement took place during a Media Freedom Coalition strategic workshop in Oslo, ahead of a November sitting of Parliament where media reform is expected to feature.
The discussion connects legal protections with a second, equally urgent question: how independent newsrooms can build sustainable businesses while serving the public.
The coming legislative process will show whether those ambitions can become durable institutions and practical protections.

sectionDescription: The people, traditions and creative voices giving Botswana its rhythm.
title: Dithubaruba: where living heritage takes centre stage
excerpt: At Molepolole’s celebration of Kweneng heritage, dance, poetry and food become a meeting place for generations.
imageAlt: Traditional dancers performing at the Dithubaruba cultural festival
author: BWIRE Culture
body: Dithubaruba is more than a festival programme. It is a meeting place where memory, identity and performance move between generations.
The Molepolole celebration of Kweneng cultural heritage brings together traditional dance, poetry, contemporary music and food. Each offers a different way into a shared story.
For younger participants, the festival creates room to encounter tradition as something active and evolving rather than fixed behind glass.
That exchange is the event’s enduring power: heritage is not simply displayed, but practised, questioned and carried forward.

sectionDescription: The people, traditions and creative voices giving Botswana its rhythm.
title: Domboshaba keeps culture in motion
excerpt: A new generation of performers is finding fresh energy in the rhythms, regalia and collective spirit of the festival stage.
imageAlt: Dancers in blue tops performing together at Domboshaba festival
author: BWIRE Culture
body: At Domboshaba, culture arrives with movement. The festival stage brings performers and audiences into the same circle of rhythm, call and response.
The event has become a meaningful platform for cultural expression, with music and dance creating connections across age and experience.
Its contemporary relevance lies in that participation. Tradition is renewed each time a young performer learns a step, a song or the story behind it.

sectionDescription: Digital life, innovation and the technology changing how Botswana works.
title: Digital skills push opens new doors for young Batswana
excerpt: Training programmes are connecting practical technical skills with entrepreneurship, mentorship and routes into the digital economy.
imageAlt: Young people attending a digital innovation workshop
author: BWIRE Digital Desk
body: Botswana’s digital ambitions increasingly depend on a practical question: how quickly can people gain the skills to participate in new industries?

Training initiatives centred on coding, digital entrepreneurship and workplace readiness are helping to turn access into opportunity. The strongest programmes pair technical instruction with mentorship and connections to real projects.
For young people, the value is not only a certificate. It is the confidence to build, test and present an idea — and a clearer path towards earning from it.
The next challenge is scale, so that opportunity reaches beyond a small group of urban early adopters.

sectionDescription: The athletes, clubs and competitions carrying Botswana’s sporting ambition.
title: Tebogo marathon gives sport a purpose beyond the finish line
excerpt: The inaugural charity marathon links a national sporting icon with breast cancer awareness and community fundraising.
imageAlt: Letsile Tebogo interacting with supporters after a race
author: BWIRE Sport
body: The inaugural Letsile Tebogo Charitable Foundation marathon combines a community sporting event with Breast Cancer Awareness Month activities.
A cancer awareness symposium was planned alongside the race, with proceeds directed towards the foundation’s charitable work.
The event shows how the profile of elite sport can be used to bring people together around public health and community support.
Its success will be measured not only at the finish line, but in the awareness and practical assistance it helps generate.

sectionDescription: The essential national stories, clearly reported and put in context.
title: New council to coordinate Botswana’s malaria elimination push
excerpt: A national council will bring partners together around prevention, surveillance and the long-term goal of elimination.
author: BWIRE Newsroom
body: President Duma Boko has launched a council intended to drive and coordinate Botswana’s malaria elimination efforts.
The initiative brings a clearer governance structure to work that depends on sustained surveillance, prevention and cooperation across public health partners.
Elimination requires consistency between outbreaks as well as rapid action when cases emerge. The council’s role will be to keep that long-term work coordinated and visible.

sectionDescription: Arguments and perspectives that interrogate the issues shaping Botswana.
title: Diamonds built our present. Imagination must fund our future.
excerpt: The new development fund is an important start, but diversification will be judged by the opportunities it creates beyond the balance sheet.
imageAlt: A satellite view of the Orapa area in central Botswana
author: BWIRE Editorial
body: Botswana’s diamond story has never only been about minerals. It is a story about what a country can build when natural wealth is matched with institutions and long-term thinking.

The Diamonds for Development Fund opens another chapter. Its initial capital matters, but its greater significance lies in the recognition that the next economy cannot simply be a continuation of the last.

Diversification is often discussed as a list of sectors. It is more useful to think of it as a wider distribution of capability: more people able to build companies, more ideas reaching markets and more communities connected to productive opportunity.
That requires patient capital, transparent decisions and a willingness to back experimentation without lowering the bar for results.
The fund should be judged by what becomes possible because it exists — new enterprises, resilient jobs and export capacity that outlives its first announcement.
keyPoints: Diversification must expand capability, not only change sector labels.
Transparent project selection will be essential to public confidence.
Success should be measured in durable enterprises and jobs.
